itemListElement.name: Gojo vs Raycast: MacBook notch controls or a keyboard-first launcher?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Raycast is an extensible keyboard-first launcher and command interface. Gojo is a MacBook-notch control surface with a more focused built-in utility set.

mainEntity.name: Do Gojo and Raycast both manage windows?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Raycast offers keyboard-driven window movement, resizing, custom commands, and layouts. Gojo includes window snapping as one notch control.

mainEntity.name: Can Gojo and Raycast run together?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Raycast centers on keyboard commands, while Gojo centers on a hoverable MacBook notch. Check and adjust shortcuts if your configuration overlaps.

mainEntity.name: Which is better for clipboard history?

acceptedAnswer.text: Raycast includes clipboard history as part of its launcher feature set. Gojo includes clipboard history for people who want that access inside the notch.

blocks.label: Short answer
blocks.copy: Choose Raycast if your workflow begins with a keyboard shortcut, search, commands, extensions, snippets, and automation across apps and services. Choose Gojo if you prefer a hoverable MacBook-notch surface for glanceable controls such as media, windows, clipboard, files, calendar, battery, webcam, and Night Shift.
points: Best specialist fit: keyboard-first commands, search, extensions, snippets, and app automation.
Best Gojo fit: pointer-friendly, glanceable controls that live near the MacBook notch.
Use both if Raycast runs command workflows and Gojo handles quick visual controls.

content.s: Raycast is stronger when the keyboard is the center of the workflow. It is built for launching, searching, commands, snippets, AI, extensions, and configurable actions.
Gojo is stronger when the interaction should be visual and close to the notch. It keeps media, windows, clipboard, files, calendar, battery, webcam, and display controls in a compact surface.
Use Raycast for keyboard-first commands and integrations, then use Gojo for quick visual or pointer-accessible controls in the notch.

Comparison pages are only useful if they are honest about scope. Gojo is a MacBook notch utility, not a blanket replacement for every specialist app. Before granting macOS Accessibility, Automation, Camera, Calendar, or other permissions to any utility, check whether the requested access matches the feature you plan to use.
